# Initialize-ZbxAgentHost

## SYNOPSIS

Creates the host, interface and items an agent session answers, or reuses those that exist.

## SYNTAX

### Session (Default)

```
Initialize-ZbxAgentHost [-Session] <string> [[-HostName] <string>] [-HostGroup <string>] [-InterfaceAddress <string>] [-InterfacePort <int>] [-ValueType <ZabbixItemValueType>] [-PassThru] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### Spec

```
Initialize-ZbxAgentHost [[-HostName] <string>] -Key <string[]> [-HostGroup <string>] [-InterfaceAddress <string>] [-InterfacePort <int>] [-ValueType <ZabbixItemValueType>] [-PassThru] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

The Initialize-ZbxAgentHost cmdlet makes sure the server has the host an agent answers as, in -HostGroup, with one agent interface (-InterfaceAddress and -InterfacePort) and one item per key: each key the session named in -Session answers, or each key in -Key. A passive session gets Zabbix agent items, which the server polls on that interface (its port is the session's listener port unless -InterfacePort is given), and an active one active checks; a second run reuses what exists, by host name and then by item key, and adds only what is missing. A new item's value type is the built-in key's own (agent.ping Unsigned; agent.version, agent.hostname and system.uname Character, as Zabbix's own agent templates have them) and -ValueType for every other key: Text unless given, which stores whatever a handler answers; give Unsigned or Float for a key that answers numbers you want to graph. With -Session, what was created is remembered on the session for Get-ZbxAgentHost, Publish-ZbxAgentHost and Clear-ZbxAgentHost; the command writes the host's status only with -PassThru.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Create a host with agent items from a list of keys

```powershell
Initialize-ZbxAgentHost -HostName 'web-02' -Key 'app.health', 'app.version' -HostGroup 'Web servers' -ValueType Character -PassThru |
    ForEach-Object Items
```

Creates web-02 (host group -HostGroup, created if missing; 'PowerShell agents' when omitted), one agent interface (127.0.0.1:10050 unless -InterfaceAddress/-InterfacePort) and one active item (ZabbixActive, every 1m) per key. -ValueType applies to every new item but a built-in key's (Text when omitted). -PassThru writes the resulting host status.

### Example 2: Publish what a running agent answers

```powershell
Start-ZbxActiveAgent -Name 'web-agent' -Hostname 'web-02' -Server 'zabbix.example:10051'
Register-ZbxActiveAgentHandler -Name 'web-agent' -Key 'app.health' -ScriptBlock { 'ok' }
Initialize-ZbxAgentHost -Session 'web-agent' -HostGroup 'Web servers' -PassThru | ForEach-Object Items
Get-ZbxItem -Host 'web-02' | Select-Object Key, ValueType | Sort-Object Key
Stop-ZbxActiveAgent -Name 'web-agent'
```

With -Session, the keys are the session's own: the built-in four plus every registered handler (HasLocalHandler), and the host name defaults to the session's -Hostname. The built-in keys get their own value types and app.health Text, so every item takes the answer it is sent (for a handler that answers numbers you want to graph, add -ValueType Unsigned or Float). The agent's own requests log 'host not found' until the server's configuration cache loads the new host (up to CacheUpdateFrequency, 60 s by default).

### Example 3: Run it again safely

```powershell
Initialize-ZbxAgentHost -HostName 'web-02' -Key 'app.health', 'app.uptime' -HostGroup 'Web servers' -WhatIf
Initialize-ZbxAgentHost -HostName 'web-02' -Key 'app.health', 'app.uptime' -HostGroup 'Web servers'
Get-ZbxItem -Host 'web-02' | Select-Object Key, Type | Sort-Object Key
```

Idempotent by host name and item key: a second run reuses the host, interface and items that already exist and only adds what is missing (here app.uptime); nothing is reshaped. -WhatIf shows the host it would touch.

### Example 4: Let the server poll a passive agent

```powershell
Start-ZbxPassiveAgent -Name 'web-agent' -Hostname 'web-02' -AllowedPeer '10.0.0.0/24' -Port 30150
Register-ZbxPassiveAgentHandler -Name 'web-agent' -Key 'app.health' -ScriptBlock { 'ok' }
Initialize-ZbxAgentHost -Session 'web-agent' -HostGroup 'Web servers' -InterfaceAddress '10.0.0.7' -PassThru | ForEach-Object Items
Stop-ZbxPassiveAgent -Name 'web-agent'
```

A passive session's keys become Zabbix agent items, which the server polls on the interface: its port is the session's listener port, and -InterfaceAddress is where the server reaches this machine (an IP address, or a DNS name the server resolves). The agent answers only the peers -AllowedPeer lets in, so it names the server's network.

### -InterfaceAddress

The address the server reaches the agent interface on: an IP address, or a DNS name the server resolves. A passive agent is polled there, so it must be the address of this machine as the server sees it. Default: the address a passive session's listener is bound to when it is bound to one, otherwise 127.0.0.1.

### -ValueType

Value type for a newly created item whose key is not a built-in one. Default: Text, which stores any answer; give Unsigned or Float for keys that answer numbers, to graph them. The built-in keys always get their own (agent.ping Unsigned; agent.version, agent.hostname and system.uname Character). Ignored for an item that already exists.
